unit.title: Weather, Travel and the World Around Us

theory.title: Weather, seasons and what is happening now
theory.explanation: Use the present simple for typical or repeated weather: It often rains in autumn. Use the present continuous for weather happening now: It is raining at the moment. Use in before seasons and weather adjectives after be: It's sunny, cold or windy. Ask What's the weather like? to find out about the weather.
theory.tip: Remember the difference: It rains a lot here (usual) and It's raining now (happening at this moment).

patterns.label: Block 1 · Typical weather
examples: It is usually warm in spring.

patterns.label: Block 2 · Weather now
examples: It is raining at the moment.

patterns.label: Block 4 · Seasons
examples: The days are short in winter.

patterns.label: Block 7 · Clothes for weather
examples: I'm wearing a coat because it's cold.
Take an umbrella. It's wet outside.

patterns.label: Block 9 · Frequency
examples: It hardly ever snows in my town.

patterns.label: Block 10 · Simple plans
examples: Let's stay inside because it's raining.
We can go for a walk when it is sunny.

content.passage: Here is the weather for tomorrow. In Edinburgh, it will be cold and cloudy, with a temperature of six degrees. It often rains there in autumn, so take an umbrella. In London, it will be sunny in the morning and warm in the afternoon. Cardiff will be windy, and it may rain after lunch. In Manchester, it is snowing now, but the snow will stop this evening. The warmest place tomorrow will be London. Remember your coat if you go out early!

content.audioTranscript: Good morning. Here is today's weather. In the north, it is cold and cloudy, and it is raining in Glasgow. The temperature is seven degrees. In the south, the sun is shining and it is warm in London, at fifteen degrees. It is windy on the coast, so take a coat. Tomorrow will be colder, and there may be snow in the hills. Summer is usually warmer and drier than spring. Have a lovely day.
